items.title: В Азербайджане можно будет переводить деньги между разными банками через одно приложение
items.summary: Headline only: users in Azerbaijan will be able to send money between different banks from one app. The launch date and rails are not stated.
items.idea: We could add cross-bank transfers to any Azerbaijani bank account inside the Birbank app, starting with a pilot on the instant payment rails, to reach customers of other banks.

dependencies: CBA rules and participation terms for instant payment system access by non-member flows
Agreement and technical interface with other Azerbaijani banks
Core transfer system integration and fraud controls
risks: Scope depends on the actual rails; the source gives only a headline
Other banks may decline or delay participation
Existing transfer by phone number and to local bank accounts already cover part of the need, so the gain may be smaller
sim.pilot: Map which Azerbaijani banks are reachable on the instant payment rails and run a limited pilot with one partner bank.
sim.mechanism: Birbank users pick a recipient bank account from a list of Azerbaijani banks and send money via the instant payment rails from inside the app, with the recipient matched by phone number or card where the other bank supports it.
sim.segment: Existing Birbank users who regularly pay people banking with other Azerbaijani banks, plus new users who want one app for cross-bank transfers.

items.title: Fonepay, Nabil Bank launch digital payment app for foreign visitors
items.summary: Fonepay and Nabil Bank launch a digital payment app for foreign visitors in Nepal. Only the headline is available.
items.idea: We could build a tourist-facing QR payment mode in the Birbank app that lets foreign visitors pay at local merchants with a foreign card, to grow Non-cash transactions.

dependencies: Card scheme and acquirer support for QR payments from foreign cards
CBA FX and cross-border payment rules
Bir Pay QR acceptance network in Azerbaijan
risks: Small visitor base in Azerbaijan, so volumes stay low
Source gives only a headline about a Nepal launch, so the model is an assumption
Overlaps with Click to Pay and Apple Pay for foreign cards
sim.pilot: Test foreign-card acceptance at a few Baku tourist merchants that already accept Bir Pay QR, and measure approval rates.
sim.mechanism: A tourist mode in the Birbank app would let a foreign-card holder scan a merchant QR code and pay in the local currency, with conversion shown before confirmation.
sim.segment: Foreign visitors and expatriates in Azerbaijan holding foreign cards, including tourists from neighbouring markets.

items.title: Banks Target Recurring Payments to Win More Card Spending
items.summary: Several banks have launched tools that manage recurring card payments. U.S. Bank's Payment Switch moves subscriptions to its cards in the app, Citi and Mastercard's Smart Subscriptions launched in the UAE, and Kiwibank in New Zealand became the first to offer Visa's Recurrent, which shows recurring charges and lets customers stop them.
items.idea: We could add a recurring-payments view to the Birbank app that lists card subscriptions with merchant, amount and frequency, and a one-tap option to move them to a new card. Start with the card-switch flow, since it targets monthly active users.

dependencies: Merchant data and recurring-payment tokens available to the card system
Existing linked services and subscriptions feature as a base
Card scheme rules for moving merchant tokens between cards
risks: Merchants may not support token migration, which limits the card-switch flow
Overlap with the existing linked services and subscriptions feature needs a clear new capability
Customers may see the feature as a reminder to cancel and not as spending growth
sim.pilot: Build the read-only subscriptions list for a small group of card holders first, then add the card-switch flow for two merchants.
sim.mechanism: A recurring-payments screen in the Birbank app would list card subscriptions with merchant, amount and frequency, and offer a one-tap move of selected subscriptions to another Birbank card.
sim.segment: Card holders with several recurring online subscriptions, such as streaming, software and telecom services.
